project_metadata.job_description:
I'm looking for an experienced Mechanical Design Engineer with strong SolidWorks skills to help develop a mechanical product from concept through manufacturing-ready CAD.

This is a real product development project—not simply creating a 3D model. I'm looking for someone who understands engineering principles, manufacturing methods, tolerances, and Design for Manufacturing (DFM).

The ideal candidate has experience designing products that have progressed from concept to prototype and production.

Scope of Work:
• Develop complete 3D CAD model in SolidWorks
• Create parametric parts and assemblies
• Design functional mechanical components
• Optimize for DFMA
• Create production-ready engineering drawings
• Apply GD&T where required
• Select standard hardware and fasteners
• Perform tolerance analysis
• Advise on manufacturing processes
• Support prototype revisions

Deliverables:
• SolidWorks Part (.SLDPRT)
• SolidWorks Assembly (.SLDASM)
• STEP files
• Engineering drawings (PDF & DWG)
• Exploded assembly views
• Bill of Materials (BOM)
• Manufacturing-ready documentation
• Source files
Preferred Experience
• SolidWorks

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], thank you for putting together such a thorough proposal! Your technical experience, particularly your focus on DFMA and GD&T, really caught my attention. Many freelancers only provide quick renders, whereas I need a design that can be manufactured reliably.

Here are the answers to your questions:
Manufacturing Process: The production version will be plastic injection molded using ABS or a PC/ABS blend. Before that, we need functional prototypes produced through 3D printing (FDM/SLA) to test the mechanism. The design therefore must be optimized for injection molding while still being straightforward to print for testing.
Internal Hardware: Yes, the device contains a custom PCB measuring approx 65mm x 40mm x 12mm, a 18650 Li-ion battery holder, a small servo motor, and an internal latch mechanism.
Operating Environment: This is a handheld consumer device intended for indoor/light outdoor use. It requires clean ergonomics and drop protection capable of meeting 1.2m drop test resistance.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: My budget for this first CAD and manufacturing-preparation milestone is $200. Within that amount, can you include the main housing 3D CAD, internal mounting features, a basic tolerance check, and an initial set of drawings?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],
Thank you for providing all of those details. The requirements are well defined, and using injection molding for production together with FDM/SLA printing to validate the prototypes is a sensible strategy.

Yes, the $200 budget can include the primary housing CAD, internal mounting provisions for integrating the PCB, battery holder, and servo, plus an initial tolerance assessment and drawing package.

My deliverables for this phase would be:

• A complete 3D CAD model covering the housing and its internal structure
• Mounting features for the PCB, battery, and other hardware
• Production ready STEP files suitable for prototyping and manufacturing review
• Preliminary engineering drawings showing key dimensions and assembly information
• A basic DFM assessment for injection molding that addresses wall thickness, draft angles, and assembly considerations

After the design has been reviewed and prototype-tested, we can apply any required changes before proceeding to the final manufacturing documentation.

Please share the PCB files, dimensions, and any mechanical references you have available. I can examine everything and begin immediately.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
[FREELANCER_NAME_001], this is an excellent breakdown and exactly what I needed. I especially appreciate the detailed explanation of the DFM feedback report and draft analysis, since that should prevent thousands in tooling adjustments later.
I’ve attached the DXF containing the PCB board outline, as well as a rough hand-drawn sketch showing the latch arrangement and the preferred overall aesthetic.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Let’s create the contract at $200 based on the deliverables listed above. How long do you estimate this stage will take to finish?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Great, and thank you for the update!

Before starting, I noticed that the DXF, hand sketch, and reference pictures you referred to have not appeared on my side. When you have a chance, could you resend those files? As soon as they arrive, I’ll review the full package and begin right away.

**Project Timeline (3 Business Days)**

**Day 1**
• Establish the overall 3D architecture
• Confirm the fitment of the PCB and battery
• Build the primary enclosure shell in SolidWorks

**Day 2**
• Create the internal latch mechanism
• Incorporate ribs, bosses, and mounting features
• Conduct draft angle analysis and tolerance checks
• Provide progress screenshots/3D views for your feedback

**Day 3**
• Complete the final CAD model
• Produce the STEP files
• Create 2D engineering drawings containing the BOM and key dimensions
• Finish the DFM review
• Submit the complete final project package

Please send the Upwork offer for the $200 milestone. I’ll start immediately once the milestone has been funded and the project files have been received.

messages.text:
